sections.title: Joseph and Potiphar's House
observations: Joseph is sold into slavery in Egypt, but he quickly gains favor in Potiphar's house due to his hard work and integrity.
This section highlights God's providence in Joseph's life, as he rises to a position of responsibility despite his circumstances.

sections.title: Joseph and Potiphar's Wife
observations: Potiphar's wife attempts to seduce Joseph, but he resists her advances, demonstrating his commitment to God and his master.
Joseph's refusal is a key moment that illustrates the importance of moral integrity and faithfulness.

sections.title: Joseph's False Accusation and Imprisonment
observations: After Joseph rejects Potiphar's wife's advances, she falsely accuses him of attempted rape, leading to his imprisonment.
This event underscores the theme of suffering for righteousness' sake and foreshadows Joseph's eventual vindication.

sections.title: Joseph in Prison
observations: Even in prison, Joseph finds favor with the warden, who entrusts him with the care of other prisoners.
This section reinforces the idea that God is with Joseph, providing him favor and success even in dire circumstances.

importantVerses.commentary: The Lord was with Joseph, and he became a successful man. This verse emphasizes God's presence and blessing in Joseph's life, despite his hardships.
How then can I do this great wickedness and sin against God? Joseph's response to temptation highlights his understanding of sin and his commitment to God.
But the Lord was with Joseph and showed him steadfast love. This verse reassures readers of God's unwavering presence and love, even in suffering.

questions: What does Joseph's response to temptation teach us about integrity and faithfulness?
How can we understand God's providence in our own difficult circumstances?
What lessons can we learn from Joseph's experiences in Potiphar's house and in prison?
